tree_shrub.name: Tree & Shrub Protocol
notes: Track rotation by IRAC/FRAC group and active ingredient. Merit, Zylam, and IMA-jet all count as Group 4A/neonic-style pressure.
Snapshot 2.5TG is the quarterly bed pre-emergent. Match the rate to the target weed and labeled site; treatment history determines whether an application is due.

CRM ordinance zone is required. Sarasota/Venice and Manatee/Parrish landscape N/P blackout runs June 1-Sept. 30. North Port turf blackout starts April 1, but landscape plants are route-gated separately. Unknown zone defaults to Sarasota/Manatee conservative.
Palm/tree injections are add-ons only. Minimum $35/palm, not included in Tree & Shrub tiers.
Do not make oil + copper, oil + broad-spectrum pyrethroid, or neonic systemics a default production tank. Use plant safety, pollinator status, pest ID, and life stage gates.

Waves palm fertilizer chart: width × width ÷ 105 lb, rounded down to one decimal (6 ft = 0.3 lb, 8 ft = 0.6 lb, 10 ft = 0.9 lb, 12 ft = 1.3 lb, 14 ft = 1.8 lb, 16 ft = 2.4 lb, 18 ft = 3.0 lb, 20 ft = 3.8 lb). Weigh each palm separately and spread evenly under the canopy, never piled at the trunk, off hardscape and 10 ft from water. This is the company canopy chart, distinct from the bag directions. Keep feedings about 3 months apart, at most four per year; count both palm fertilizers together.

Palm scout every visit, and record only what you see (symptom + photo, never a disease name without a diagnosis): oldest fronds with translucent yellow-orange spots or dead tips (potassium) or a broad yellow band (magnesium); newest fronds small and frizzled (manganese, mainly queen, royal, pygmy date); a collapsed spear or bronzing from the oldest fronds up; a hard shelf/conk on the lower 4-5 ft of trunk; fronds dying down one side; royal palm bug, spiraling whitefly, scale, or sooty mold; over-pruning.

Palm diagnosis-only issues: suspected lethal bronzing, Ganoderma butt rot, or Fusarium wilt gets a photo, a note, and a call to the owner that it needs a diagnosis; do not quote a treatment on symptoms, and never promise the fertilizer program prevents them. Lethal-bronzing injections are preventive only, for healthy palms, palms near an infected one, or palms that tested negative; a symptomatic, positive, or infected palm is handled outside the injection service. Do not cut off potassium-yellowed fronds (it speeds decline; old fronds never re-green, new growth recovers over 1-2+ years), and never prune above the 9-to-3 o'clock line.

pest.name: Pest Control Protocol

field_rules.ask: What do I do first at a pest stop?
field_rules.rule: Knock on the door. Then walk around the outside of the home and inspect it.

field_rules.ask: Do I treat inside or outside first?
field_rules.rule: Ask the customer. Do first the part that the customer wants first.

field_rules.ask: What is the order of work outside?
field_rules.rule: First sweep the webs and the wasp nests. Then apply the Taurus band. Then apply Talak.

field_rules.ask: What do I sweep?
field_rules.rule: Sweep webs and wasp nests from the eaves, doors, windows and lanai. Do this on every visit.

field_rules.ask: Which sprayer do I use outside?
field_rules.rule: Use the FlowZone backpack for Taurus and for Talak. Use a different backpack for each product. If you have one backpack, rinse it before you change the product.

field_rules.ask: When do I use the B&G sprayer?
field_rules.rule: Use the B&G sprayer for inside treatment and for mud dauber nests. Do not use it for other outside work.

field_rules.ask: How much Taurus per gallon?
field_rules.rule: Mix 0.8 fl oz Taurus SC in 1 gallon of water. This is 0.06%. Do not mix Taurus and Talak in the same backpack.

field_rules.ask: Where does Taurus go? How much mix?
field_rules.rule: Spray Taurus on the foundation only. Make the band 1 ft up the wall and 1 ft out on the ground. Use 2 quarts of mix for each 160 ft of wall. A home with 200 ft of wall needs about 0.5 fl oz of Taurus.

field_rules.ask: Can I use Taurus again?
field_rules.rule: Apply Taurus a maximum of 2 times each calendar year at each home. Apply it in the rainy season, June to September. After 2 applications, do not apply Taurus at that home until the next year.

field_rules.ask: How much Talak per gallon?
field_rules.rule: Mix Talak 7.9 F at 0.5 fl oz per gallon of water. Do not add LESCO 90/10 or a different surfactant.

field_rules.ask: How wide is the Talak band?
field_rules.rule: Spray Talak in a band 6 ft wide around the home. Use a maximum of 10 gallons of mix for each 1,000 sq ft. Wait 7 days or more between applications at the same home.

field_rules.ask: What do I spray on the eaves, the lanai and the garage?
field_rules.rule: Use the same Talak mix on the eaves, the lanai or pool cage and the garage. In the garage, spray the door thresholds and the corners. Do this on every visit.

field_rules.ask: Can I spray Talak on an ant trail?
field_rules.rule: Do not spray Talak on an ant trail. The spray breaks up the colony and it spreads. Put bait on the trail.

field_rules.ask: It is raining. Can I spray Talak?
field_rules.rule: Do not spray Talak in rain.

field_rules.ask: Is Talstar P a rotation from Talak?
field_rules.rule: Talak, Talstar P and Bifen I/T are the same chemical, bifenthrin. A change between them is not a rotation. Record all three as Talak.

field_rules.ask: Can I use Alpine outside?
field_rules.rule: Do not use Alpine WSG outside. The only exception is a mud dauber nest.

field_rules.ask: How do I treat mud daubers?
field_rules.rule: Treat mud dauber nests with Alpine WSG in the B&G sprayer.

field_rules.ask: Do I put granules down?
field_rules.rule: Do not apply granules on a normal pest visit.

field_rules.ask: Do I treat inside?
field_rules.rule: Treat the inside on every pest visit. Do not treat inside if the customer says no.

field_rules.ask: Where do I treat inside?
field_rules.rule: Treat the kitchen, the bathrooms, the doors, the windows and other entry points. Also treat each place where the customer reports pests.

field_rules.ask: How do I apply Alpine inside?
field_rules.rule: Inside, apply Alpine WSG with the B&G sprayer. Apply it only to cracks, crevices and voids. Do not fog.

field_rules.ask: How much Gentrol?
field_rules.rule: Mix Gentrol at 1 fl oz per gallon. Use it inside only, for roaches. Gentrol does not control ants or fleas.

field_rules.ask: Where does Delta Dust go?
field_rules.rule: Put Delta Dust in wall voids and weep holes. Do not put dust into an active ghost ant nest. The colony splits and spreads.

field_rules.ask: Nobody is home. What do I do?
field_rules.rule: Treat the outside only. Record that the inside was not treated. A return visit for the inside is not automatic.

field_rules.ask: The gate is locked or a dog is in the yard. What do I do?
field_rules.rule: Treat the areas that you can reach. Record the area that you did not treat and the reason. Do not schedule a return visit.

field_rules.ask: When do I complete the visit?
field_rules.rule: Complete the visit in the app before you leave the stop.

field_rules.ask: Ghost ants came back. What now?
field_rules.rule: For a ghost ant or white-footed ant callback, use bait. Do not spray more. Put sweet gel or liquid bait at each trail.

field_rules.ask: What do I look for at the slab?
field_rules.rule: Find mulch or soil that touches the slab. Tell the customer to keep a dry strip 6 to 12 in wide. Find sprinklers that hit the wall and report them.

field_rules.ask: Why are ants on the plants?
field_rules.rule: Look for aphids, scale and whitefly on plants near the home. Their honeydew feeds ants. Record the plant in the service notes.

field_rules.ask: Do I need a ladder for photos?
field_rules.rule: Take all photos from the ground. Do not use a ladder. Do not go into a locked gate, a dog yard or a closed lanai for a photo.

Essential Barrier: bifenthrin adulticide directed to foliage, fence lines, shaded resting zones, lanai perimeter, and pool cage edges
Precision Barrier: gamma-cyhalothrin adulticide for heavy vegetation, water adjacency, pool cages, and higher residual expectations
Pyriproxyfen + novaluron IGR support where breeding pressure exists

rodent.name: Rodent Control Protocol
notes: Rodent service is inspection-led. Confirm activity, entry points, sanitation pressure, and access before promising remediation.
Baiting without exclusion is monitoring, not a rodent-free structural warranty.
Use tamper-resistant stations for exterior rodenticide placements and document station count, location, and follow-up cadence.
safety_rules: Use tamper-resistant stations for exterior bait.
Do not place rodenticide where children, pets, wildlife, or non-target animals can access it.
Photo-document entry points before quoting exclusion.
Separate trapping, baiting, exclusion, and sanitation recommendations in notes.

visits.primary:
Rodent Inspection / Activity Assessment
Inspect attic, garage, roof returns, soffits, AC chase, utility penetrations, doors, weep gaps, and exterior perimeter
Document droppings, rub marks, gnawing, nesting, odor, sounds, food sources, and water sources
Photograph active or potential entry points
visits.secondary:
Classify as monitoring, trapping, baiting, exclusion, or sanitation follow-up
Set temporary monitors only when activity is unclear
Quote exclusion separately when entry points are active
visits.notes: Do not start with bait alone when active interior activity suggests a structural entry issue.

visits.primary:
Trap / Bait Station Setup
Install tamper-resistant exterior bait stations where label and site conditions allow
Set snap traps or mechanical traps in attic, garage, or utility zones when active interior movement is present
Map station and trap locations
visits.secondary:
Use non-toxic monitors when risk, access, or customer preference blocks rodenticide
Record bait type, station count, trap count, and placement areas
Schedule follow-up based on activity and customer access
visits.notes: Exterior bait stations manage pressure. Interior activity still requires trapping and entry-point work.

visits.primary:
Exclusion / Entry-Point Repair
Seal approved entry points with rodent-resistant materials
Prioritize roof returns, AC line sets, utility penetrations, gaps at doors, soffits, vents, and garage transitions
Confirm no active trapping conflict before sealing major pathways
visits.secondary:
Do not seal animals into occupied voids
Flag inaccessible or declined repairs in the customer note
Recommend sanitation or landscape trimming when pressure is recurring
visits.notes: Exclusion is a separate scope unless the estimate explicitly includes it.

visits.primary:
Follow-Up / Monitoring
Check and refresh stations or traps
Remove captured rodents or carcasses when accessible
Reinspect sealed areas and active pathways
Update activity level and customer-facing status
visits.secondary:
If activity persists, identify missed access, food/water pressure, or sanitation source
Reset cadence until activity drops to monitoring level
Escalate structural or wildlife issue if evidence does not match standard rodent pressure
visits.notes: A clean follow-up should say what changed: station activity, trap captures, new evidence, sealed gaps, and next cadence.

mosquito.name: Mosquito Control Protocol
notes: Mosquito service depends on source reduction plus directed barrier treatment. Outdoor pressure can rebuild from neighboring breeding and resting sites.
Peak SWFL pressure is typically May through October, but shaded, irrigated, or water-adjacent properties can need service outside that window.
Avoid pollinator activity and blooming plants when selecting treatment zones.
safety_rules: Wind and rain conditions must support safe application.
Do not spray open water, edible plants, blooming plants with active pollinators, or inaccessible areas.
Document standing water sources that cannot be corrected.
Use customer notes to separate source reduction from adult mosquito suppression.

visits.primary:
Mosquito Barrier Treatment
Treat shaded resting zones, foliage edges, fence lines, lanai perimeter, pool cage edges, under decks, and vegetation transitions
Use adulticide selected from inventory and label/site fit
Apply with directed backpack or approved equipment
visits.secondary:
Inspect gutters, drains, planters, bromeliads, saucers, tarps, toys, and water-holding containers
Dump standing water where practical
Document inaccessible breeding sources
visits.notes: This is the default recurring mosquito template. The customer note should mention both treatment areas and source findings.

visits.primary:
Source Reduction / Larval Support
Inspect and correct standing water sources
Apply Bti dunk tablets or approved mosquito stations where breeding sources cannot be removed
Use IGR support only where label, water source, and site conditions fit
visits.secondary:
Recheck prior breeding sources
Flag drainage, irrigation, screen, or gutter issues
Explain that adult pressure can persist when sources are off-property
visits.notes: Use this template when breeding-source pressure is the main driver, not just resting adult pressure.

visits.primary:
Event / Heavy-Pressure Mosquito Service
Inspect event-use zones, seating areas, lanai, pool deck, paths, and shaded perimeter
Treat high-use resting zones only where label, wind, rain, and pollinator conditions allow
Prioritize customer-visible use areas over blanket coverage
visits.secondary:
Set expectations for short-term knockdown versus recurring pressure
Recommend recurring mosquito plan if pressure is structural or seasonal
Document weather limits and inaccessible zones
visits.notes: Use for one-time event prep or heavy-pressure corrective visits. Do not overpromise duration.

palm_injection.name: Palm Injection Protocol
notes: Palm injections are add-ons, not default Tree & Shrub inclusions.
Diagnose the target issue before injecting. Do not use injections as a substitute for full palm fertility, irrigation correction, or disease diagnosis.
Record species or palm type, size class, product, dose, port count, target issue, photos, and follow-up timing.
safety_rules: Confirm product label and palm suitability before drilling or injecting.
Do not inject a palm with unclear diagnosis or severe irreversible decline without office review.
Disinfect equipment between palms when disease is suspected.
Document ports, dose, and follow-up date.

visits.primary:
Palm Injection Assessment
Identify palm species/type, size class, symptoms, canopy pattern, spear condition, trunk wounds, irrigation/salt stress, and fertility history
Photograph canopy, spear, trunk, root zone, and affected fronds
Determine whether Mg, Mn/Fe, systemic pest, or diagnosed disease support injection
visits.secondary:
Recommend soil/root-zone correction when injection is not the right tool
Escalate severe decline, bud rot suspicion, or unclear diagnosis before treatment
Quote injection separately from Tree & Shrub service
visits.notes: Assessment comes first. Never sell injection from a single yellow-frond observation.

visits.primary:
Palm Injection Application
Apply selected injection product per label and diagnosis
Use Palm-Jet Mg for diagnosed magnesium deficiency pattern where appropriate
Use Mn-Jet Fe for diagnosed manganese/iron deficiency pattern where appropriate
Use IMA-jet or Propizol only when pest/disease diagnosis and label fit support it
visits.secondary:
Record product, dose, port count, palm count, and application date
Keep injection work separate from routine foliar or granular Tree & Shrub work
Clean and disinfect injection equipment as needed
visits.notes: Injection pricing is per palm and should remain separate from recurring Tree & Shrub tier inclusions.

visits.primary:
Palm Injection Follow-Up
Reinspect treated palms for symptom progression, spear condition, canopy response, and new stress signs
Photograph the same angles as the assessment
Update next injection or fertility recommendation
visits.secondary:
Do not repeat injection automatically without diagnosis and timing review
Escalate non-response, worsening crown decline, or suspected pathogen issue
Document customer-facing expectations for slow visible response
visits.notes: Palm recovery is slow. Follow-up should focus on trend, not instant color change.

cockroach.name: Cockroach Control Protocol
notes: Cockroach control is species-specific. German roach work is bait, IGR, sanitation, and follow-up driven; exterior palmetto bug work is perimeter and exclusion driven.
Do not contaminate bait placements with repellent sprays.
Document sanitation, moisture, harborage, and customer prep issues clearly.
safety_rules: Confirm interior re-entry and ventilation instructions when interior products are applied.
Keep bait away from spray contamination and cleaning products.
Use monitors to verify progress on German roach jobs.
Schedule follow-up when live German roach activity is confirmed.

visits.primary:
German Roach Cleanout
Inspect kitchen, bathrooms, hinges, appliance motors, plumbing voids, cabinet seams, and food storage areas
Apply cockroach gel bait in targeted placements
Use non-repellent crack-and-crevice treatment where label allows
Apply IGR point-source or aerosol where label allows
visits.secondary:
Vacuum visible aggregation before application when practical
Place monitors and record count/location
Explain sanitation and follow-up requirements
visits.notes: Bait-first, non-repellent approach. Schedule 10-14 day follow-up for confirmed live German roach activity.

visits.primary:
American / Smokybrown / Palmetto Bug Control
Inspect exterior entry points, garage, lanai, drains, mulch, irrigation boxes, and moisture zones
Treat exterior perimeter, cracks, crevices, and harborage zones where label allows
Use granular bait in landscape or utility zones where appropriate
visits.secondary:
Interior treatment is targeted only where activity is present
Recommend door sweeps, moisture correction, drain sanitation, or exclusion when pressure is structural
Document species and likely source
visits.notes: Exterior roach pressure is usually moisture and access driven. Do not treat it like a German roach infestation.

visits.primary:
Cockroach Follow-Up
Inspect monitors, bait consumption, live activity, egg cases, droppings, and customer prep progress
Refresh bait only where consumed or contaminated
Spot treat cracks, crevices, or harborages as needed
visits.secondary:
Adjust plan if monitor counts are not dropping
Reinforce sanitation, moisture, and food-source corrections
Escalate severe or multi-unit activity for office review
visits.notes: Progress should be measured by monitor counts and live sightings, not just product applied.

bed_bug.name: Bed Bug Control Protocol
notes: Bed bug work is inspection-led and prep-dependent. Do not treat without documenting rooms, evidence, method, prep status, and follow-up plan.
Pricing and scope depend on method: chemical/IPM, heat, or hybrid. Keep quote-required cases out of generic pest workflows.
Customer prep, laundry, clutter reduction, and follow-up timing are part of the protocol, not optional extras.
safety_rules: Confirm customer prep and vacancy instructions before treatment.
Do not apply products to mattresses, furniture, or belongings unless the label explicitly allows that use.
Protect occupants, pets, aquariums, sensitive items, and heat-sensitive materials.
Schedule or recommend follow-up inspection according to the treatment method.

visits.primary:
Bed Bug Inspection / Scope
Inspect sleeping and resting areas, mattress seams, box spring, bed frame, headboard, baseboards, furniture seams, luggage zones, outlets, and adjacent rooms
Document live bugs, cast skins, eggs, fecal spotting, bites reported, rooms affected, prep status, and occupancy type
Classify method: chemical/IPM, heat, or hybrid
visits.secondary:
Photograph evidence before quoting or treating
Send prep instructions and confirm customer can comply
Escalate severe, multi-unit, or cluttered jobs for office review
visits.notes: Inspection must identify rooms affected and treatment method before any customer promise.

visits.primary:
Bed Bug Treatment
Use approved chemical/IPM, heat, or hybrid method from the estimate scope
Treat cracks, crevices, bed frame, baseboards, furniture voids, and harborages where label allows
Use dust, residual, contact, steam, vacuum, encasement, or heat steps only when included in method and label/site fit
visits.secondary:
Bag or isolate items according to prep guide
Document rooms treated, products/method, re-entry timing, and inaccessible areas
Schedule follow-up or post-treatment inspection window
visits.notes: Do not merge bed bug with general pest. This is a specialty treatment with separate prep, pricing, and follow-up.

visits.primary:
Bed Bug Follow-Up / Post-Treatment Inspection
Reinspect treated rooms and adjacent rooms
Check monitors, mattress seams, furniture seams, baseboards, and customer-reported areas
Document live activity, new evidence, or no activity
visits.secondary:
Spot treat only where label and scope allow
Reinforce laundry, bagging, clutter, and travel/luggage precautions
Escalate ongoing activity for method review or additional treatment scope
visits.notes: Follow-up determines whether the original method is working or the scope needs revision.

termite.name: Termite Control Protocol
notes: Termite protocols are compliance-sensitive. These templates define workflow and product family, while final application must follow the product label, graph/diagram, and state documentation requirements.
Keep bait, liquid, foam, and wood-treatment scopes separate because cost drivers, warranty language, and follow-up cadence differ.
Use Inventory service-product usage for COGS visibility; do not make live estimate prices depend directly on inventory quantity.

visits.primary:
Termite Inspection / WDO Support
Inspect foundation, plumbing penetrations, garage, attic access, windows, bath traps, expansion joints, and moisture areas
Document swarmers, wings, mud tubes, damaged wood, conducive conditions, and prior treatment evidence
visits.secondary:
Recommend bait, liquid, foam, or Bora-Care scope based on finding location
Collect photos before treatment proposal
Escalate active structural findings immediately
visits.notes: Inspection is the qualifying step. Treatment scope must match evidence and construction type.

visits.primary:
Termite Bait Installation / Monitoring
Install Trelona, Advance, or HexPro stations per label and site plan
Place stations around accessible perimeter and high-risk conducive zones
Record station count, spacing exceptions, obstructions, and diagram notes
visits.secondary:
Inspect stations on recurring cadence
Replace consumed bait or wood monitors as needed
Escalate active hits to treatment recommendation
visits.notes: COGS should scale with station count. Inventory service usage tracks per-station product cost.

visits.primary:
Liquid Perimeter / Trench and Rod
Termidor SC or approved termiticide per label
Treat soil at foundation, expansion joints, plumbing penetrations, and active tube zones
Diagram treated linear footage and gallons applied
visits.secondary:
Drill slab or paver zones only when required and approved
Protect wells, drains, water bodies, and inaccessible areas per label
Schedule reinspection based on activity
visits.notes: High-liability workflow. Requires exact label rate, volume, diagram, and access notes.

visits.primary:
Foam Drill / Localized Void Treatment
Termidor Foam or approved foam product into active galleries, wall voids, or localized inaccessible areas
Confirm target void, drill pattern, and customer approval before application
visits.secondary:
Patch/clean drill points where in scope
Pair with bait or liquid when structural risk is broader than localized activity
Photo before and after
visits.notes: Localized treatment only. Do not represent as whole-structure protection unless paired with a full program.

visits.primary:
Bora-Care / Wood Treatment
Apply Bora-Care or approved borate to accessible raw wood, attic members, crawlspace framing, or new construction wood
Measure treatable surface area and document inaccessible/painted/sealed areas
visits.secondary:
Protect finished surfaces and insulation
Use foam or spray method as label and access require
Recommend follow-up inspection for active evidence
visits.notes: Best for accessible wood. Cost scales by treatable sqft and dilution/application method.

visits.primary:
Annual Renewal / Warranty Inspection
Inspect stations or treated zones, conducive conditions, moisture, wood-to-ground contact, and customer-reported activity
Update diagram and photos
Confirm renewal eligibility and warranty status
visits.secondary:
Quote corrective work for conducive conditions outside warranty scope
Replace bait/monitors as needed
Schedule next inspection cadence
visits.notes: Renewal workflow protects liability and keeps the graph/current condition record clean.
